scope: Matched 64-step continuation of one published checkpoint by four arms differing only in the registration lever: detail control, the four-cell coarse-to-fine field, the same field de-meaned across the board, and the same field under a placed-target term that supervises the displacement against the cell each sample should have read. Scored read-only on the widened deciding population with the standing gates and grid, with the applied field and its image-space landing points measured from each frozen archive; no threshold, population or gate changes, and no real-image, complete-state, calibrated or quality claim.

field.note: Offsets are the ones the tap applied, in cell units, L-infinity per cell. The fraction outside its own cell is the sampling-side analogue of the oracle's wrong-target-cell coverage; a field working correctly moves samples off their nominal cell when the lattice is misplaced.

positions.note: Where the displaced samples landed, not how far they moved. in_frame is the source image; in_board is the target lattice's own 0..columns x 0..rows frame, so a shifted-window exploit at the edge shows up as a drop in one or both.

components.note: Reported, never read by the verdict: ranking at each arm's own best boundary, the cost of the fixed 0.0 boundary, and the cost of transferring a boundary chosen on the other eleven ancestry groups, each with the interval that resamples exactly it and a minimum detectable effect at 80% power.

power.rule: minimum detectable effect = 2.802 x cluster SE

placed.question: Does supervising the displacement - telling the field which cell each sample should have read - make per-cell registration pay where occupancy-only supervision of the same field did not?
placed.reading_text: Supervising the displacement does not clear the attribution floor over the free field, so neither occupancy-only nor placed-target supervision of this field makes per-cell registration pay. The objective class is what fails, not the reach, the bound or the field.
